description: Highlights of My Week at the Capitol As we approach the last few weeks of the legislative session, significant bills are being brought to a vote in their respective chambers. Despite the busy schedule here at the Capitol, I have prioritized making time for phone conversations with anyone who reaches out. Recently, I had the opportunity to speak at an event for the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM), where I discussed the TRAP Bill currently in progress in the house, particularly addressing concerns HR professionals may have regarding changes to training agreements statewide. At the event, I was able to speak about how these trainings can be very beneficial, and that what we are doing here will not affect that. Thank you SHRM for the invitation to speak. While typically I refrain from delving into the politics of it all in the recaps, this week I'll provide insight into my voting decisions and the thought process behind them. HB24- 1292- Prohibit Certain Weapons Used in Mass Shootings Last week, I wrote about an organization that caused a lot of noise in my office, this is the bill that was the catalyst. If passed, this bill will ban the manufacturing and sale of assault rifles in Colorado. It was extremely difficult to decide my vote on this bill because I honestly believe that this bill has issues that will cause an immediate and massive influx of assault weapon purchases between now and July 2025 when it goes into effect. I’m also a police officer, an armorer for these types of weapons, as well as a former law enforcement firearms instructor - so I have many biases that affect how I think of this legislation. However, as my title and job is "Representative", I will always represent the people in my district. I’ve heard from many many many of you directly who have wanted this legislation, so I voted Yes. I was honestly thankful that I wasn't a swing vote, and even more thankful for the people that have contacted me all day today to share stories and those who appreciated where I stand. Now it is in the Senate to start the process over. I still have reservations - and I took all the actions that I know to take to resolve those concerns, but now I have a bit more gray hair and my thoughts are with the Senate as they confront this legislation.
title: HD-37 Newsletter
